reviews.evidence: Created and read the complete foundation. The core retains both defining conditions: separability and existence of a metric whose metric-induced topology is the given topology and which is complete, explicitly distinguishing existence of one such metric from completeness of every compatible metric. Direct targets complete-metric-space, separable-space, and metric-induced-topology define those conditions. Examples were checked for every n≥0: ℝⁿ is Polish; an interval (a,b) with a<b is Polish via a homeomorphism to ℝ despite its usual metric being incomplete; ℚ is separable but not completely metrizable by the Baire-category obstruction. Root repaired stripped LaTeX escapes, made a,b finite real endpoints explicit, and checked transported metric completeness directly through the isometry h; Q is nonempty meagre without isolated points, contradicting Baire.
